# Plain Metal's generateMipmapsForTexture: on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 26.7, 25G229): 2D textures,
# arrays and cubes whose first level is wider or taller than 64 texels (share-mips-m3, our own
# probe). Each chain ran Private (written and read by blits) and the 256x256 BGRA8Unorm one of nine
# levels Shared and again Private too, byte-identical. The first level of every layer, in turn,
# comes from one splitmix64 stream seeded by the FNV-1a 64 hash of the chain's key: `u8` random
# bytes (each the top byte of one draw), `h16` halves `((r >> 40) % 16) << 10 | (r & 0x3ff)`, `f32`
# floats `(100 + (r >> 40) % 28) << 23 | (r & 0x7fffff)`, `ramp` (x, y) and `xramp` x and `yramp` y
# of each texel's coordinates as floats. Each level's digest is the first 12 hex digits of the
# SHA-256 of its bytes, every layer in turn, rows tight; level 0's is the first level as generated
# (and read back unchanged).
# Format:
#   <key> <format> <2d|2darray|cube> <width>x<height> <layers> <pattern> <digest of level 0> ...
